takeaways.label: Lumpy quarter, H2 confidence intact
takeaways.text: Q2 FY27 revenue fell below the recent trend as only 5–6 of 9 commercial CMS molecules shipped, but management kept H2 and FY28 growth expectations unchanged, citing the strongest RFP pipeline to date.

takeaways.label: Peptide block commissioned, revenue still 1.5–2 years out
takeaways.text: The new peptide facility at Unit One is operational and seeing traction, but PPQ-related revenues are 6–9 months away and first commercial shipments are 1.5–2 years out; idle-time costs will be borne by Neuland in the interim.

takeaways.label: Gross margin slipped on input costs
takeaways.text: Gross margin declined to 59.4% from 60.1% YoY as geopolitical conflicts drove raw material price volatility and higher freight and logistics costs.

takeaways.label: Land bank expanded for the long term
takeaways.text: The company acquired ~134 acres at Kakinada with first right of refusal on another ~60 acres, and the board approved additional land around Unit I; management flagged Kakinada as a long-duration investment with no near-term returns.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the specialty segment normalizes by Q4 as guided, the pace of peptide project progression toward PPQ, and any further input-cost escalation.

points.label: Revenue composition
points.text: Q2 revenues were driven predominantly by commercial CMS molecules and Prime portfolio products within GDS; only 5 or 6 of the 9 commercial molecules contributed, with some smaller intermediates shipping just once every 2–3 years.

points.label: No launch drop-off
points.text: The unevenness is attributed to timing and product-mix variability in commercial CMS shipments, not to any reduction in launch quantities; the last launch was about a year ago and no new launches occurred in the last 2–3 quarters.

points.label: H1 in line
points.text: Despite the Q2 softness, H1 FY27 was largely consistent with expectations, and management reiterated that the business must be assessed over longer periods.

points.label: Specialty segment drag
points.text: A few molecules that contributed significantly in the past saw customers struggle with manufacturing, which hit revenues; normalization is expected by Q4 based on customer feedback.

points.label: Working capital stretched
points.text: Working capital days rose to 104 from 84 QoQ, driven by the changing scale and composition of the business; management is focused on inventory, collections, and aligning working capital requirements.

points.label: Input cost pressure
points.text: Geopolitical conflicts drove volatility in certain raw material prices and escalation in freight and logistics costs through H1.

points.label: Staff cost step-up
points.text: Q2 staff costs moved up substantially, partly for the peptide unit, with further additions expected in regular R&D and at manufacturing sites for peptides and other APIs.

quotes.text: Davuluri: "As individual commercial shipments become larger, a shift in timing can have a greater impact on quarterly revenues, and that is why we keep saying lumpiness, quite often in our earnings calls and conversations. This makes growth uneven from a quarter-to-quarter basis, and that is why we keep saying that we need to assess our business over longer periods."

points.label: Module 1 commissioned
points.text: The new peptide block at Unit One is operational, configured with 3 DAC columns (2 of 60 cm) and a lyophilizer sized to match the current portfolio of peptide projects.

points.label: Revenue timeline
points.text: Development-related peptide revenues are already being billed but are not substantial; PPQ-related revenues are expected in 6–9 months, with MSA and first commercial batch shipping in another 6–9 months after PPQ, putting actual commercial revenues roughly 1.5–2 years out.

points.label: Idle-time costs
points.text: The facility was built for a portfolio of projects; a couple are moving forward and expected to use it, but idle time is anticipated over the next 1–1.5 years and Neuland will bear those costs.

points.label: Module 2 planning
points.text: Configuration and investment for Module 2 are not yet crystallized; the goal is to finalize and move forward in the next 3–6 months.

points.label: Investment resilience
points.text: Management stated that Modules 2, 3, and 4 will be triggered if Module 1 gets occupied, and even a negative impact on the current CMS business would not halt peptide investments because of sustained demand for peptide API.

points.label: Full API capability
points.text: Neuland intends to make the complete peptide API, including fragments, crude, purification, and final isolation; fragment-making is a core capability the company plans to capitalize on.

points.label: Manufacturing complexity
points.text: Peptide synthesis is irreversible: unlike small molecules where you can reprocess to remove an impurity, in peptides you may have to junk the entire reactor, so precision is critical at large scale and in downstream manufacturing.

quotes.text: Davuluri: "The Module 2, Module 3, Module 4, which is the peptide investment, will get triggered if Module 1 gets occupied and if we have some kind of negative impact in our current CMS business or commercial business, we would still continue with those investments because we believe that there is a sustained demand for peptide API."

points.label: RFP activity at a high
points.text: The level of RFP activity in FY27 has been the strongest to date, stemming from relationships built over several years.

points.label: Big pharma penetration
points.text: Meaningful headway has been made in establishing relationships with big pharma; several proposals are the result of sustained efforts to build new customer relations.

points.label: Molecule selectivity
points.text: The company is far more selective than a decade ago; it used to do generic CDMO work such as exclusive generic API for a client but no longer enters those discussions, and the pedigree of clients has shifted toward big pharma.

points.label: Molecule size growth
points.text: Management hardly used to see a ₹100 cr molecule until five years ago; today they see numerous ₹100 cr molecules and have even seen ₹1,000 cr molecules.

points.label: DMF filings
points.text: Two DMFs were filed in Q2: Fezolinetant and Ivacaftor, strengthening the GDS portfolio.

points.label: NDA and IND support
points.text: The company supported 1 additional NDA filing and has 9 IND filings in the pipeline.

points.label: Patent cliff insulation
points.text: The three large CMS/CDMO products have no patent expiries in meaningful markets before 2030, and management is fairly certain the post-2030 dip will have no impact on the growth trajectory, which will come from peptides, complex small molecules, and other products.

quotes.text: Davuluri: "I think we are fairly certain that there will be no impact because of the dip from these molecules on the growth that is going to come, which... will not just be from peptides, there will also be complex small molecules, there will be other products as well."

points.label: Kakinada land acquisition
points.text: Approximately 134 acres were acquired at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, for future expansion, with first right of refusal on an additional ~60 acres that could take the total to ~200 acres over the next two years.

points.label: Long-term return profile
points.text: Management urged investors to view Kakinada as a long-duration investment with no returns in the immediate timeframe; if there were an impact on commercial products, Kakinada would likely be slowed before peptides.

points.label: Unit I expansion
points.text: The board approved investment to add more land around Unit I, expanding its footprint.

points.label: Process R&D center
points.text: A new center at Genome Valley, Hyderabad, is expected to be fully operational by early next year; it is a process development center for small molecules and peptides, not new modalities like oligonucleotides, ADCs, or HPAPIs.

points.label: Integrated development model
points.text: The R&D center will combine process design, process engineering, quality by design, flow chemistry, and integrated development capable of generating small volumes of API in one paperless, highly automated location, replacing the prior model where process design happened in R&D and then moved to a pilot plant at a manufacturing site.

quotes.text: Davuluri: "I would probably urge investors to look at the investment in Kakinada more from a long-term return perspective rather than something that will give us returns in the immediate timeframe."

points.label: Overcapacity cycle expected
points.text: Management expects the GLP-1 euphoria to drive overcapacity, then testing, then correction, which it views as normal for any thriving industry.

points.label: Capabilities over reactors
points.text: Players who merely install reactors and expect customers to do technology transfer may face challenges when those customers leave; those with strong R&D capabilities in peptides can cater to the roughly 1,000 synthetic peptide drugs beyond any single weight-loss molecule.

points.label: India capacity gap
points.text: There is still very little peptide CDMO capacity in India relative to small molecules; no overcapacity exists in India, though there may be in China.

points.label: Talent scarcity
points.text: India does not have enough CDMO peptide talent; there is talent for generics but not for CDMO, and this is a challenge.

points.label: Lumpiness as a scaling artifact
points.text: As the business has scaled, the size of large opportunities has increased almost in proportion, so lumpiness persists; management’s intent is to break away by adding more projects, but if even larger opportunities are attracted, lumpiness may remain and is not necessarily a bad thing.

quotes.text: Davuluri: "Lot of players who are just putting in reactors and expecting customers to come and do the technology transfer, I believe that they may face more challenges because the moment that customer goes away they only are sitting with equipment and not necessarily capabilities, but if you have strong R&D capabilities in peptides, then you are also able to cater to these other 1000 molecules."

items.title: Group growth guide
items.text: Management has "always aspired to grow at about 20%" and expects FY27 and FY28 to grow at that rate, with the 18-20% CAGR called "a fair assumption" over five years. At ~₹2,307 cr TTM revenue, that implies adding roughly ₹400-450 cr of revenue a year, supported by a 25%+ EBITDA margin plan.

items.title: Peptide facility module 1
items.text: Module 1 of the new commercial peptide facility at Unit 1 (7,000 L reactor capacity, three DAC columns, two lyophilisers) went operational in September 2026, part of a ~₹250 cr peptide investment lifting peptide capacity from 0.5 KL to 6.37 KL. PPQ revenues are expected within six to nine months and commercial peptide revenues in roughly 1.5-2 years, with modules two to four (module two up to 18,000 L) triggered once module one fills.

items.title: CMS commercial molecule ramp
items.text: Commercial CMS is the primary near-term driver: H1 FY27 commercial CMS revenue was ₹639 cr vs ₹411 cr a year earlier, with growth anchored on about three active molecules, no meaningful patent expiries before 2030, and one more commercialization expected in FY27. Unit 3, running at only 30-40% utilization, added 215 KL in FY25 enabling scale-up of a key product from 50 MT to 150 MT, leaving substantial volume headroom as ramps continue.

items.title: Gland Pharma sterile API partnership
items.text: Announced 5 August 2026, a long-term CDMO partnership under which Gland Pharma will build a dedicated sterile API suite at Visakhapatnam for microparticle depot products, adding ~1,400 kg of annual capacity to USFDA/EU standards. The asset-light arrangement pairs Neuland's complex API chemistry with sterile manufacturing it does not own, opening a differentiated product category with management seeing scope beyond the initial few products.

items.title: Unit 1 capacity additions
items.text: The Board approved adding 120.5 KL to Unit 1 (91% utilized) for ₹143.4 cr over 12-18 months, plus a further 18 KL for ₹39.8 cr within 6-7 months, and commercial production of earlier Unit 1 and Unit 3 expansions commenced 31 July 2026. Six to seven acres of adjacent land have also been acquired, letting Neuland add capacity faster than greenfield approval cycles would allow.

items.title: Genome Valley R&D center
items.text: A ₹189 cr, 140,000 sq ft process R&D center at Genome Valley is set for inauguration, with full operation expected by early next year, tripling current R&D space and adding integrated process engineering, flow chemistry and dedicated peptide labs. Combined with the new peptide plant, management says this lab-to-commercial chain "would probably not be matched by many Indian CDMOs," supporting conversion of the 99-project CMS pipeline.

items.title: GDS specialty filings
items.text: Two US DMFs were filed in H1 FY27 (fezolinetant, ivacaftor) after six filings in FY25 including Difelikefalin, Neuland's first peptide DMF, alongside a GLP-1 molecule in development. Each filing feeds the shift from low-margin Prime toward higher-margin Specialty products, while FY26 revenue grew 37% to ₹2,053 cr at a 29.4% EBITDA margin, driven by commercial CMS projects.
